title: The two and the one beyond (15.16–15.20)
word: The two and the one beyond
hook: the perishable, the imperishable, and the highest person beyond both

segments.voice: Yesterday: the light in the sun. Sun, moon, fire, the fire in your belly, and the light seated in every heart. Your line, in Krishna's voice, was I am the light. Today, the chapter's last and shortest teaching. Day two hundred twelve.
screen: `THE LIGHT IN THE SUN — I AM THE LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Look at a wave. It rises, curls, crashes, and it's gone. Now look at the ocean under it. The ocean doesn't crash. It was there before this wave, and it'll be there after. So there are two things: the wave that passes and the water that stays. Chapter fifteen doesn't stop there. In five short verses, it says there are two, and then there's a third, beyond both. And it ends the chapter with a claim: know this, and you've done what you came to do.
screen: `THE WAVE THAT PASSES.` → `THE WATER THAT STAYS.` → `AND ONE BEYOND BOTH.`

segments.voice: Verse sixteen. There are two persons in this world, the perishable and the imperishable. Kshara, the perishable, is all beings: every body, every life that begins and ends. Akshara, the imperishable, is called kutastha, the one that stands firm, unchanging. Verse seventeen: but the highest person is another, called the supreme self, the undying Lord who enters the three worlds and holds them up. Verse eighteen: because I am beyond the perishable, and higher even than the imperishable, I am known in the world and in the Veda as Purushottama. The highest person. Purushottama is still a name for Krishna and for Vishnu. Here, the schools read carefully and differently. For Ramanuja and his school, the three are real and distinct: changing beings, unchanging souls, and the Lord beyond and within both. For Advaita teachers, the highest person is the one reality, and the other two are how it appears to us. Then verse nineteen: whoever, free of confusion, knows me as the highest person, knows everything, and worships me with their whole being. And verse twenty ends the chapter: this is the most secret teaching, Arjuna. Knowing this, a person becomes wise, and has done all there is to do. Just five verses, and the chapter calls itself the most secret teaching. That's why its last word to you is short: know this. That's the word today: the two and the one beyond.
screen: `THE PERISHABLE: ALL BEINGS.` · `THE IMPERISHABLE: UNCHANGING.` · `BEYOND BOTH: THE HIGHEST PERSON.` · `KNOW THIS, AND YOU'VE DONE IT.` · then, large: `THE TWO AND THE ONE BEYOND.`

segments.voice: Sit, and notice what's changing. The breath, in and out. Sounds arriving and leaving. Thoughts passing. That's the perishable. Now notice what hasn't changed since you sat down: the plain fact of being aware. That's closer to the unchanging. Then, without trying to picture anything, rest your attention on whatever holds both. You don't have to name it. Just let the sitting be wide enough to include it. The bell holds the time.
The two and the one beyond. Gita fifteen: the perishable and the imperishable, and beyond both, Purushottama, the highest person.
screen: `THE TWO AND THE ONE BEYOND — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: know this. Today, when something ends, a meeting, a song, a day, notice for one breath that something in you watched it end and didn't. Day two hundred twelve.

howItsDone: Purushottama, the highest person, is a name of Krishna and Vishnu; some Hindus memorize Gita chapter fifteen, which names Purushottama near its close, and recite it whole.

match.prompt: the two and the one — tap the pairs.

myth: Gita 15 names only two persons: the perishable and the imperishable
verse 17: the highest person is another, beyond both.
beyond the perishable, higher even than the imperishable.
every school reads the three the same way
Ramanuja's school reads three real, distinct realities; Advaita reads one reality appearing as the others.

fork.setup: chapter fifteen ends. what does Krishna say happens to the one who knows this teaching?
options: they must still study all the Vedas.
they become wise and have done all there is to do.
fork.reveal: verse 20: knowing this, a person becomes wise, and has done what is to be done.

original.note: Sanskrit: purushottama, purusha (person) + uttama (highest): the highest person, Gita 15.18.

trapdoor: what you thought: there's the world, and there's God.
what it means: Gita 15 names the perishable, the imperishable, and the highest person beyond both.
what a scholar hears: kshara, akshara (called kutastha) and purushottama in 15.16–15.18; Vishishtadvaita reads them as three real categories, Advaita reads the highest as the one reality.
